title: Plans for tomorrow
goal: Talk about the future, make plans, and negate something that hasn't happened yet.
bekal: lay out a plan in several steps with a clear time order

dialogs.title: حِوَار — قَبْلَ السَّفَرِ
dialogs.intro: Budi is going home to Indonesia next month. Laila asks about his plans.

lines.speaker: لَيْلَى:
lines.id: When are you going back to Indonesia?

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.text: سَأُسَافِرُ فِي الشَّهْرِ الْقَادِمِ، إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ.
lines.id: I'll be leaving next month, God willing.
lines.literal: will-I-travel in the-month the-coming, if willed God.

lines.speaker: لَيْلَى:
lines.id: And what will you do there?

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.text: سَأَعْمَلُ فِي شَرِكَةٍ، وَسَأُدَرِّسُ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ فِي الْمَسَاءِ.
lines.baca: sa'a'malu fii sharikah, wa sa'udarrisul-'arabiyyata fil-masaa'.
lines.id: I'll work at a company, and teach Arabic in the evenings.
lines.literal: will-I-work in company, and will-I-teach the-Arabic in the-evening.

lines.speaker: لَيْلَى:
lines.text: فِكْرَةٌ مُمْتَازَةٌ! هَلْ سَتَعُودُ إِلَى مِصْرَ؟
lines.baca: fikratun mumtaazah! hal sata'uudu ilaa Miṣr?
lines.id: Great idea! Will you come back to Egypt?
lines.literal: idea excellent! will you-return to Egypt?

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.text: أَتَمَنَّى. سَوْفَ أَعُودُ بَعْدَ سَنَتَيْنِ لِلدِّرَاسَةِ الْعُلْيَا.
lines.baca: atamannaa. saufa a'uudu ba'da sanataini lid-diraasatil-'ulyaa.
lines.id: I hope so. I'll come back in two years for my master's.
lines.literal: I-hope. will I-return after two-years for the-studies the-higher.

lines.speaker: لَيْلَى:
lines.id: You won't forget your Arabic, will you?

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.baca: abadan! sa'aqra'u kulla yaumin wa sa'uraasiluki.
lines.id: Never! I'll read every day and I'll write to you.
lines.literal: never! will-I-read every day and will-I-write-to-you.

lines.speaker: لَيْلَى:
lines.id: All right. When shall we meet before you leave?

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.text: يَوْمَ الْخَمِيسِ؟ سَأَكُونُ حُرًّا بَعْدَ الظُّهْرِ.
lines.id: Thursday? I'll be free in the afternoon.
lines.literal: day the-Thursday? will-I-be free after the-noon.

lines.speaker: لَيْلَى:
lines.id: Deal. I'll bring you a little gift.

lines.speaker: بُودِي:
lines.text: لَا دَاعِيَ! لٰكِنْ شُكْرًا مِنْ قَلْبِي.
lines.baca: laa daa'iya! laakin shukran min qalbii.
lines.id: You shouldn't have! But thank you from the bottom of my heart.
lines.literal: no need! but thanks from heart-my.

notes: **سَـ attaches directly, with no space.** سَأَذْهَبُ (I will go), سَتَرْجِعُ (you will return), سَنَلْتَقِي (we will meet). Notice that the verb itself doesn't change at all — its ending stays ḍammah.

**سَوْفَ is the long form, written separately.** سَوْفَ أَعُودُ. Same meaning, slightly more distant and emphatic in tone — roughly the difference between "I'll go home" and "I will definitely go home".
**لَنْ negates the future, and it turns the verb ending into fathah.** لَنْ أَنْسَى, لَنْ أَذْهَبَ, لَنْ نَرْجِعَ. The same change is triggered by أَنْ in unit 16 — the two words work as a pair.
**Notice that لَنْ doesn't take سَـ.** Writing لَنْ سَأَذْهَبَ is a mistake; the negator itself already carries the future meaning.

**إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ is not just a polite filler.** For many speakers, mentioning a future plan without it feels improper, because the future is never considered certain. It is used by Muslims and non-Muslims alike across the Arab world, even in office meetings.
**سَأَكُونُ — the future of كَانَ.** "I will be". So the three tenses of "to be" are now complete: كُنْتُ (was), — (present, no word), سَأَكُونُ (will be).

**لَا دَاعِيَ — "no need, don't trouble yourself".** A polite way to turn down an offer. An equivalent: لَا تَتْعَبْ نَفْسَكَ ("don't wear yourself out"). Declining without a phrase like this can come across as cold.

grammars.title: The future: سَـ and سَوْفَ
after: If the sentence already has a future time word (غَدًا, اَلْأُسْبُوعَ الْقَادِمَ), سَـ is often simply dropped: غَدًا أَذْهَبُ إِلَى السُّوقِ. This is very common in conversation, much like English "Tomorrow I'm going to the market".
Three tenses, three forms you now fully control: **ذَهَبْتُ** (I went) · **أَذْهَبُ** (I go) · **سَأَذْهَبُ** (I will go).

grammars.title: لَنْ — negating the future
after: The whole A1 system of Arabic negation is now complete: **لَيْسَ** (no verb) · **لَا** (present) · **مَا / لَمْ** (past) · **لَنْ** (future). Four tools, four situations, no overlap.

blocks.text: لَمْ أُقَرِّرْ بَعْدُ ("I haven't decided yet") uses the لَمْ you know from unit 13, plus بَعْدُ, meaning "up to now". The pattern لَمْ ... بَعْدُ is the standard way to say "not yet" in Arabic — much like English "haven't ... yet", there is no single word for it.

blocks.title: Time and certainty in the Arab world
items: In many Arab countries, appointment times are read more loosely than in Japan or Germany. This isn't a personal trait but a social habit.

The most useful way to deal with it isn't to complain but to confirm: the day before, send a short message — هَلْ مَا زَالَ مَوْعِدُنَا غَدًا؟ ("are we still on for tomorrow?"). This one sentence saves many afternoons.

blocks.text: Farewells for someone about to travel: رِحْلَةً سَعِيدَةً ("have a good trip"), فِي أَمَانِ اللهِ ("in God's safekeeping"), and the warmest of all — لَا تَنْسَنَا ("don't forget us"). The traveler answers: لَنْ أَنْسَاكُمْ أَبَدًا.

exercises.prompt: Put into the future with سَـ.

items: What will you do there? (to a man)

exercises.prompt: Write your plans for the next six months, in at least six sentences using سَـ, سَوْفَ and لَنْ.

answers: سَأَذْهَبُ — سَنُسَافِرُ — سَيَعْمَلُ — سَتَدْرُسِينَ — سَيَرْجِعُونَ — سَأَكُونُ
لَنْ أَذْهَبَ إِلَى السُّوقِ. — لَنْ تَنْسَى الدَّرْسَ. — لَنْ نُسَافِرَ غَدًا. — لَنْ يَرْجِعَ فِي الْمَسَاءِ. — لَنْ أَكُونَ مَشْغُولًا.
سَأُسَافِرُ فِي الشَّهْرِ الْقَادِمِ. — مَاذَا سَتَفْعَلُ هُنَاكَ؟ — لَنْ أَنْسَى الْعَرَبِيَّةَ. — مَتَى سَنَلْتَقِي؟ — لَمْ أُقَرِّرْ بَعْدُ. — رِحْلَةً سَعِيدَةً!

Example: سَأَعْمَلُ فِي شَرِكَةٍ جَدِيدَةٍ — سَأُسَافِرُ إِلَى مِصْرَ فِي الصَّيْفِ — سَوْفَ أَتَعَلَّمُ الْخَطَّ الْعَرَبِيَّ — لَنْ أَتْرُكَ الدِّرَاسَةَ — سَأُقَابِلُ أَصْدِقَائِي الْقُدَامَى — كُلُّ هٰذَا فِي السَّنَةِ الْقَادِمَةِ، إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ
